content_units: Broad 1995–2015 pop culture trivia, balanced across   movies, TV, music, video games, and internet culture  , with difficulty increasing from Round 1 to Round 5. This set includes   5 rounds of 8 questions  , plus   1 final tie-breaker  .
1   Familiar hits   Easy   Mainstream across all categories
2   Recognizable details   Easy-Medium   Slightly deeper recall
4   Deep fan territory   Medium-Hard   More specific references
5   Specialist pop culture   Hard   Tough cross-category finish
1. In  Titanic  (1997), what is the name of Leonardo DiCaprio’s character?
2. Which TV sitcom features Ross, Rachel, Monica, Chandler, Joey, and Phoebe?
3. Which singer released the 2008 hit single “Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)”?
4. What handheld game series features creatures such as Pikachu, Squirtle, and Charmander?
5. What video-sharing website, launched in 2005, became famous for user-uploaded clips and viral videos?
6. In the  Harry Potter  films, what house is Harry sorted into at Hogwarts?
7. Which animated TV show features the characters Stan, Kyle, Cartman, and Kenny?
8. Which singer was known as the “Princess of Pop” in the late 1990s and early 2000s?
Round 2: Familiar, But a Little Deeper
1. In  Mean Girls  (2004), what day is jokingly celebrated by fans because of a line from the film?
2. Which mockumentary-style U.S. workplace sitcom premiered in 2005 and is set at Dunder Mifflin?
3. Which OutKast song includes the repeated line “Hey ya!” and became a massive hit in 2003?
4. What game console did Nintendo release in 2006 that used motion controls?
5. What early social networking site was famous for customizable profile pages and a default friend named Tom?
6. In  The Matrix  (1999), does Neo take the red pill or the blue pill?
7. Which reality competition show began in 2002 with the phrase “You’re fired”?
8. Which 2000s singer had hits with “Since U Been Gone” and “Behind These Hazel Eyes”?
1. In  The Dark Knight  (2008), which actor played the Joker?
2. Which TV drama premiered in 2004 with the survivors of Oceanic Flight 815 stranded on a mysterious island?
3. Which 2011 Adele album features the songs “Rolling in the Deep” and “Someone Like You”?
4. What 2004 Blizzard game became one of the most influential MMORPGs of all time?
5. What does the “Rickroll” prank trick people into watching?
Answer:   Rick Astley’s “Never Gonna Give You Up”
6. In  Shrek  (2001), what is the name of the kingdom ruled by Lord Farquaad?
7. Which teen drama starred Blake Lively as Serena van der Woodsen and premiered in 2007?
8. Which singer interrupted Taylor Swift’s acceptance speech at the 2009 MTV Video Music Awards?
1. In  Inception  (2010), what object does Cobb use as his totem?
2. Which TV series featured the fictional ad agency Sterling Cooper and later Sterling Cooper Draper Pryce?
3. Which singer released the 2007 album  Back to Black ?
4. In  Halo: Combat Evolved , what is the name or military rank by which the main protagonist is best known?
5. What was the name of Google’s social network launched in 2011?
6. In  Napoleon Dynamite  (2004), what animal does Kip and Napoleon’s brother Rex not own, but Uncle Rico tries to discuss selling?
(Acceptable if host prefers: this may be asked as the animal Napoleon draws—also   liger  .)
7. Which sci-fi TV revival began in 2005 with Christopher Eccleston as the Ninth Doctor?
1. In  Scott Pilgrim vs. the World  (2010), how many evil exes must Scott defeat?
2. Which TV show ended in 2014 with the final episode titled “Felina”?
3. Which producer’s tag “another one” became a widely recognized internet catchphrase in the mid-2010s?
4. In  The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , what instrument does Link use to travel through time-linked events and trigger songs?
5. What was the name of the 2007 Apple device widely credited with redefining the modern smartphone era?
6. In  Donnie Darko  (2001), what is the name of the man in the creepy rabbit suit?
7. Which cult NBC sitcom, created by Dan Harmon, is set at Greendale Community College?
8. Which 2000 Gorillaz song shares its title with a Clint Eastwood reference and features the line “I ain’t happy, I’m feeling glad”?
In what year was the first  YouTube  video, “Me at the zoo,” uploaded?
- Print tip: Put only the questions on team sheets and keep the answers on a host master copy.
- Hosting tip: Award   1 point per correct answer  , then use the tie-breaker only if teams are tied for first.
- Optional pacing: 8–10 minutes per round, 2–3 minutes to score between rounds.
